### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name), meta.getItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:name; the route ledger binds it to GET /meta/:type/:name))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getPublished (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/published; the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name/published))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleMetadataRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via meta.saveItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:name; the route ledger binds it to PUT /meta/:type/:name), saveItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.saveItem, bound to PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.saveItem, bound to PUT /meta/:type/:name))_
- `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx`  _(via getItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.getItem, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via deleteItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.deleteItem, bound to DELETE /api/v1/meta/:type/:name), meta.deleteItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to DELETE /api/v1/meta/:type/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:name), meta.saveItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name, selected by route anchor /meta/:type/:name; the route ledger binds it to PUT /meta/:type/:name), saveItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.saveItem, bound to PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name; the bare tail of client method meta.saveItem, bound to PUT /meta/:type/:name), /:type/:name/published (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItemLayered — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type/:name (route, 35 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **154** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3bbf05955e9391397e8c1dc7c567dd86aff5935f` — the merge of head `c71460ec1b137b9c5187df435797596eb499f72f` into base `4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3bbf05955e9391397e8c1dc7c567dd86aff5935f && git checkout 3bbf05955e9391397e8c1dc7c567dd86aff5935f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca c71460ec1b137b9c5187df435797596eb499f72f && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca && git merge --no-ff c71460ec1b137b9c5187df435797596eb499f72f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4c29f38447e17d4109a0141792ed2b8dace3ddca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c71460ec1b137b9c5187df435797596eb499f72f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-query-decision.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-meta-door-closed-sets.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-item-query-decision.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts, .changeset/26699-layered-read-member.md, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts `readMetaItem` (the item GET's member steps, `:10681-10690`, `:11032-11042`), `resolveBundleMemberSelector` / `bundleMemberDiscriminator` / `memberOption` (`:2670-2755`), `findServedOverlayRow` (`:10339-10375`), `packagelessReadAddress` (`:16931`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-artifact-lookup.ts (`lookupArtifactItem`, member narrowing `:63-77`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/overlay-index.ts (`overlayMemberValue` / `overlayMemberWhere` `:518-546`), packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts `metaItemQueryRefusal` / `repeatedOnceRefusal` / `metaMemberSelector` / `createMetaLayeredAnswer` (absent → refuse), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts `serveMetaItemLayered` (`:4190-4250`), packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts `answerMetaLayered` / `queryRefusalAnswer` / the `/layers` branch (`:880-930`, `:963-968`, `:1175-1212`), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts `layered()` (`:1655-1659`), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs and scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (`judgeLevel`, `none-baseline-moved`), .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml (`Metadata-protocol` kind table, `:782-820`), lint.yml / ci.yml job mapping for the two exit-3 gates.

Reviewer of record: `session_01WGufzgbJhFoXYsLSe5WSPP`, an isolated subagent of the owning seat. Read on 2026-10-27 between 19:02Z and CHECKS_FINAL_TIME: card #26699 (body + all 5 comments: 6444245782, 6445712655, 6446804626, 6448343327, 6450890318), #26649's ruling record 6444406836 and os-dev-report 6442702169, rulings 6116165299 (#22877 A) and 6138588561 (#23072 B), PR #26861 body, file list (14 paths), its one comment (6450870662, docs-drift bot), the net diff against `main` at the head (705 lines; merge-base `0ea90c7a1`), and the head's 45 check-runs (three readings: 19:02Z, 19:12Z, CHECKS_FINAL_TIME). The head had not moved at any reading.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The layered read names the member exactly as the item GET does — PASS.** `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema.member` (`protocol.zod.ts:726`) is `z.string().optional()` described by the same `BUNDLE_MEMBER_SELECTOR_DESCRIPTION` the get / delete / publish / history requests share, so the five requests cannot drift. On the wire it is `META_ITEM_MEMBER_PARAM` (`'member'`), read through the one `metaMemberSelector(query)` on both doors (`rest-server.ts:4215`, `meta.ts:1210`). The value is judged once, by `resolveBundleMemberSelector(request.type, request.member)` (`protocol.ts:11356`), the same call `readMetaItem` makes (`protocol.ts:10686`): the per-type discriminator comes from `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` via `bundleMemberDiscriminator`, a selector on a type with no discriminator, a blank one and one over 100 characters are the same located `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with the same sentence. **One closed-set decision, not forked:** `META_ITEM_QUERY_DOORS.layers` is `{ accepted: META_ITEM_LAYERS_PARAMS /* ['package','member'] */, once: ['package','member'] }` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:2316`); RestServer's `/layers` route now asks `metaItemQueryRefusal('layers', req.query)` (`meta-item-read-routes.ts:363`) where it used to call `refuseUnknownQueryParams(req, res, META_ITEM_LAYERS_PARAMS)` — recognition and arity were split across two helpers before; the dispatcher asks the same function at `meta.ts:1180`. This diff REDUCES the fork ruling 6138588561 B was about (the member's arity rule now lives only in the shared decision). The residual `refuseRepeatedQueryParams(req, res, ['package'])` in `serveMetaItemLayered` (`rest-server.ts:4205`) is pre-existing, redundant after the shared decision for the dedicated route, and still the arity rule for the deprecated `?layers=` spelling — harmless, not this card's.

**2. Absent / unknown / undiscriminated member — PASS.**
- *Absent member, byte-identical for every existing caller of a type with no discriminator:* `member` is `undefined` → `wantedMember` is `undefined` → `isWantedMember` is constantly `true`, `namedMemberOnly` passes everything through, `lookupArtifactItem(type, name, pkg, undefined)` equals the old 3-arg call (`protocol-artifact-lookup.ts:63-77`: the 4th argument is forwarded as `undefined`), `registry.getItem(…, undefined)` likewise, `memberOption(undefined)` is `{}` and `packagelessReadAddress(type, name, undefined)` is the old call. The callers I read — `plugin-security` (`permission`, `:83`, `:194`), the `/published` door (`meta-item-history-routes.ts:1281`), the `?layers=` spelling (`rest-server.ts:3674`) — pass no member and address undiscriminated types or the canonical member. **One deliberate non-identity, flagged by the dev (Acceptance notes ¶1):** for an `email_template` whose `MetadataService` copy is a non-canonical member, the bare layered read's `code` layer used to be that copy and now falls to the canonical artifact (`protocol.ts:11389`, `if (isWantedMember(fromService.data))`). That is the correction ruling 6116165299 Q2-i requires (absent = the canonical member, "which is what the registry's bare-name read answers") and is exactly what `readMetaItem` already does (`protocol.ts:11032-11042`); the old answer was the defect. Unpinned (the objectql harness has no `MetadataService`) — see ③.
- *Unknown member → 404, never the canonical member:* the artifact lookup is asked at `wantedMember` and the answer kept only if `isWantedMember(artifact)` (`protocol.ts:11443-11445`); the registry's answer is dropped unless it is the named member (`namedMemberOnly`); the overlay `where` carries `bundle_member = value` through `overlayMemberWhere` (`overlay-index.ts:543`); `packagelessReadAddress` takes the member. Every layer therefore answers `null` for `fr-FR`, `createMetaLayeredAnswer` refuses `{ reason: 'absent' }` when no layer is present (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:3892`), and both transports answer their plain 404 (`rest-server.ts:4240` via `sendMetaReadRefusal`; `meta.ts:915`). Pinned on the real engine (`environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts:706`, all four fields `null`) and on both transports with a double (`meta-item-query-decision.test.ts:545-552`).
- *Member on a type with no discriminator:* refused by `resolveBundleMemberSelector` before any read, with `status` and `code` asserted — `expectSelectorRefusal` asserts `err.status === 400` and `err.code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` (`:351-352`) on the real protocol for `view`, and the runtime test asserts `400` + `VALIDATION_ERROR` + the sentence on the dispatcher AND on a real `RestServer` route handler driven against a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` (`:554-587`), with the spy proving the refusal happened inside the protocol. A repeated `member` is one refusal on both transports (`:516-522`), and the `?layers=`+`member` rule 3 refusal is untouched (`LAYERED_VIEW_MEMBER_MESSAGE`, `meta-item-read-gate.ts:2375`).

**3. The layers returned for a non-canonical member are that member's — PASS, read in the implementation path.** `code`: the service copy only when `itemDiscriminator(type, copy) === wantedMember`; else the artifact at `wantedMember` (`registry.getArtifactItem(singular, name, pkg, member)`, `protocol-artifact-lookup.ts:76`); else the registry entry for `member`, dropped if another member answers. `overlay`: `findServedOverlayRow({ …, ...memberOption(member) })` → `overlayMemberWhere(type, member)` → the row whose `bundle_member` is the named value (`null` for the canonical, `overlay-index.ts:522`), at the package `packagelessReadAddress(type, name, member)` resolves for that member. `effective` derives from those two. The lock layers (`artifactLockLayerAt`, `overlayLockLayerAt`) stay at the request's address with no member, exactly as `readMetaItem`'s do (#21761 / #21803: the strictest lock among the item's rows in scope) — the same choice the item GET made, not a leak of another member's content. Pinned: `zh-CN` answers `code: 'PKG zh', overlay: 'ADMIN zh', effective: 'ADMIN zh'` beside a stored `en-US` row; a member stored by nobody answers its own code layer and `overlay: null` (`:181-193`); CONTROL the whole `en-US` answer equals the bare answer (`:202-203`). The ablation leg (drop `...memberOption(member)`) reddening exactly the `zh-CN` and `fr-FR` cases is coherent with this reading: without the member the overlay `where` falls to the canonical row.

**4. Client SDK `layered()` — PASS to leave unchanged.** `MetadataClient.layered(type, name, options: { packageId?: string } = {})` (`ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts:1655-1659`) is untouched; no `layered` exists under `packages/client/src`. Ruling 6444406836 assigns "the editor passes `member` to its layered and draft reads" to the ONE UI PR on #26649, so changing it here would cross the card's `⛔ the ui half (#26649)` fence; the dev checked it and recorded the carrier (out_of_scope_findings[0]). Right.

**5. Declarations — `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added` STAND for this diff; the ruling record's `none` does not.** The claim 6448343327 and PR body carry `Clause-②: yes` (bare: a widening — `clause2-line.mjs:111-112`, both spellings take at least `minor`) and `Metadata-protocol: added`; ruling record 6444406836 on #26649 spelled the child card `Metadata-protocol: none` inside its `Workload:` estimate line, before any diff existed. For THIS diff `added` is the only lawful spelling: the diff moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` (+`api/GetMetaItemLayeredRequest:member`), and the level axis in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (`judgeLevel`, `:2054-2055`) refuses `none` over a moved `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard as `none-baseline-moved`, exit 1 — in its own words "a changed authorable-surface shard is an authorable key added or removed". The ratchet's definition of the authorable surface includes the `api/` request schemas, and `protocol.zod.ts`'s `GetMetaItemLayeredRequest` IS what a protocol client writes against. The maintainer's letter A ruled the behaviour (the selector extends to the layered read); the `Workload:` line's kind was the director seat's pre-diff estimate, not part of the ruling, and the gate's reading of the actual tree supersedes it. `Check Changeset` (pr-automation `changeset-check`, which runs this axis on the PR body and changeset) is green on the head. `Clause-②: yes` is right: `META_ITEM_LAYERS_PARAMS` widens from one name to two, and `@objectstack/spec`'s declared request widens by an optional key. Carrier check: both lines are line-initial in the PR body (`:9-10`) and in the changeset body (`:10-11`), same spelling.

**6. Skills-docs line — PASS.** `git grep -n "/layers\|getMetaItemLayered\|META_ITEM_LAYERS" c71460ec1 -- skills/ .claude/skills/` → 0 hits, as claimed; no skill or ADR lists the member-selector doors either (`?member=`, `member selector`, `BUNDLE_MEMBER` → 0 hits under `skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `docs/adr/`). The two hand-written pages that name `/layers` (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx:192`, `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx:366`) describe the save-verdict gate, not the route's parameters — read, confirmed. `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` is generated (one row, the description verbatim). Nothing hand-written becomes false.

**7. Regenerations — PASS.** `protocol.mdx` gains the one row for `member`; `api.json` gains `api/GetMetaItemLayeredRequest:member` in sorted position. The spec regeneration gates ran on the head: `check:generated --reconcile-only` and `check:authorable-surface` in `Type Check · source gates` (success, 19:00:59Z), `check:api-surface` in `Type Check · consumer gates` (success, 19:05:09Z), `Spec property liveness` (success, 18:54:40Z).

**8. The dev's two exit-3 derived gates and the ablation leg, judged against the check-runs.** `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` runs in ci.yml `Build Core` (`:3069`) → **success, 19:06:36Z**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-examples` runs in lint.yml `Type Check · consumer gates` (`:6488`) → **success, 19:05:09Z**. Both NOT-MEASURED locals are measured green on the head; the dev's "CI runs both on the PR" was right. The ablation is a local measurement no check-run repeats; I did not re-run it (read-only). Its shape is coherent with the implementation path (judgment 3), the restore is recorded (`git diff HEAD` empty, preflight `--absent` exit 0, 34/34), and the red leg is "as expected" in the only sense that counts: the two tests that red are the two that depend on the mutated spread. Accepted as reported evidence, not as a verified measurement.

**9. The head's test gate is RED — `Test Core (6/8)` = `failure`, and the record cannot exclude this diff as its cause — FAIL.** Check-run 122402055950 (`Test Core (6/8)`, completed 19:16:58Z) failed in step 11 "Run this shard's tests"; its two failure annotations read `command (/home/runner/work/objectstack/objectstack/packages/plugins/plugin-security) …/pnpm run test exited (1)` and `Process completed with exit code 1.` The job log itself could not be read from this container: the Actions log store (`productionresultssa19.blob.core.windows.net`) is policy-denied by the session's egress proxy (CONNECT 403 at 19:17Z), and the MCP log reader returns only the last ~5,000 lines (19:10:39Z onward — `@objectstack/cli`'s run, 129 files / 1615 tests green), which end after the plugin-security run. So the failing test is unidentified here. What IS readable: (a) `@objectstack/plugin-security` holds two live callers of the changed method — `packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts:83` and `security-catalog-echo.ts:194`, both `{ type: 'permission', name }` — and `security-catalog-echo.test.ts:246` / `:257` drive a REAL `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` through `getMetaItemLayered`; (b) my reading of the path says those calls are byte-identical (judgment 2: undiscriminated type → `wantedMember` undefined → every new guard is a pass-through, every new trailing argument is `undefined`); (c) the dev's local full-suite runs covered spec, metadata-protocol, rest, runtime and one objectql file — `plugin-security` was never run against this diff (os-dev-report `tests`), and the 109 dispatch-gate families are check scripts, not package tests; (d) the base this head merged, `4c29f3844`, had all seven planned `Test Core` shards green (18:52Z), so the red is new on this head. A reading that says "should be identical" against a gate that says "exited 1" in exactly the package that calls the changed method is not a PASS. The gate's conclusion stands as the verdict; the record names what flips it: the failing test identified (from the job log, by a seat whose egress reaches the Actions log store, or by `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test` at this head). If it is this diff's, the fix comes with a pin in that package; if it is an unrelated or flaky red, a rerun green on this same head — or the next head — earns a fresh record, and every finding in ① 1-8, ② and ③ carries over unchanged.

**Check-runs on `c71460ec1b137b9c5187df435797596eb499f72f`.** Readings at 19:02:47Z (45 runs) and 19:12:05Z were partial (Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI in progress). Final reading 19:25:13Z, 47 runs: **38 success, 1 failure (`Test Core (6/8)`, 19:16:58Z), 7 skipped** (the opt-in / matrix-template rows: `18.x upgrade harness`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Lint UI`, and the two `${{ matrix.shard }}` template rows), **1 in_progress** — the `Test Core` aggregate job (122417196836, started 19:24:32Z after shard 5/8 completed; it summarises the eight shards, one of which is red). Every other gate named in this record is green at the stamps given: Check Changeset 18:56:12Z, Governed Surface Queue Guard 18:54:05Z, Spec property liveness 18:54:40Z, Lint & Repo Gates 19:00:36Z, Type Check · source gates 19:00:59Z, Type Check · consumer gates 19:05:09Z, Type Check · workspace 19:12:57Z, TypeScript Type Check 19:13:04Z, Type Check UI 19:16:10Z, Build Core 19:06:36Z, Build & E2E UI 19:05:31Z, Test Core 1/8-5/8 and 7/8-8/8 (last 19:24:29Z). The combined status API read `pending` at 19:02Z (no commit statuses, only check-runs). The head had not moved at 19:12Z.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime` — correct. The level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone (`clause2-line.mjs:11-13`; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3): `added` takes at least `minor` on every published package whose source the diff moves. All four are published (`private` unset, `18.2.0`) and all four have moved source in this diff (`protocol.zod.ts`; `protocol.ts`; `meta-item-read-gate.ts` / `meta-item-read-routes.ts` / `rest-server.ts`; `domains/meta.ts`). `@objectstack/objectql` moves only a test file and correctly has no entry. Not `major`: nothing is removed, renamed, refused or re-meant; every existing request shape and every existing wire answer is byte-identical except the ruling-mandated canonical correction in judgment 2. Not `patch`: a `none` declaration would be refused by the level axis over the moved `authorable-surface/api.json` shard (judgment 5). The changeset body carries both declaration lines, a summary, and no BREAKING banner (none owed: `Clause-②: yes` without `(narrowing)`). `Check Changeset` success at 18:56:12Z.
